official_sources.name: INE - Estimativas de Populacao Residente 2025 (Destaque)
official_sources.role: Revised resident population 11,424,031 at 31 Dec 2025; first fully administrative-basis estimate, with 2021-2024 revised on the same methodology. Also the source for the migrant working-age share (86.1% aged 15-64) and the foreign-resident count.
official_sources.why_it_matters: Published 22 June 2026, AFTER the 2025 annual national accounts were compiled. The accounts could not have used it, which is why Eurostat nama_10_pe still shows a 2025 national-accounts population of 10,804,160.

official_sources.name: Eurostat nama_10_pe - National accounts population and employment
official_sources.role: Total population, national concept (POP_NC) - the denominator of every published per-capita national-accounts figure, including GDP per capita in PPS.
official_sources.why_it_matters: 2025 value is 10,804,160 against a demographic estimate of 11,405,627. This documented 5.6% gap is what the whole analysis turns on.

official_sources.name: INE - GDP, 4th quarter 2025
official_sources.role: Manual anchor for 2025 real GDP volume growth

official_sources.name: Eurostat nama_10_gdp - GDP and main aggregates
official_sources.role: Nominal GDP (CP_MEUR) - the numerator of the published per-capita index

official_sources.name: Eurostat nama_10_pc - GDP per capita
official_sources.role: GDP per capita in PPS for Portugal and the EU27_2020 reference aggregate; lets the published index be reconstructed and the population inside it recovered

official_sources.name: Eurostat demo_gind - Demographic balance
official_sources.role: Resident population on 1 January and annual average. THIS is the population vintage the Commission per-capita indicators divide by, and the one the model uses

official_sources.name: Eurostat nama_10_a10_e - National accounts employment
official_sources.role: Total employment, domestic concept - compiled inside the national accounts and therefore consistent with GDP. Used to test whether the workers behind the population revision are already inside measured output

official_sources.name: Eurostat tec00114 - GDP per capita in PPS
official_sources.role: Published headline index, EU27_2020 = 100. Note this base differs from the EU27_2025 = 100 base the article quotes

official_sources.name: OECD International Migration Database (DSD_MIG@DF_MIG_EMP_EDU)
official_sources.role: Employment rate aged 15-64 by place of birth; feeds the Part IV labour sensitivity only

official_sources.name: World Bank API
official_sources.role: Long historical GDP, deflator and labour series back to 1960. Its POPULATION series is deliberately not used for modelling - it is a different vintage from Eurostat's, and that mismatch is the subject of Part I

official_sources.name: Eurostat PPP preliminary estimates methodology
official_sources.role: Confirms GDP per capita in PPS is GDP / population / PPP, which is what makes the index invertible and the correction claim testable

notes.two_population_bases: Portugal has two official 2025 populations: national accounts 10,804,160 (nama_10_pe) and demographic 11,405,627 (demo_gind / INE). Published per-capita GDP divides by the FIRST. Recover it as gdp_meur*1e6/gdp_pc_eur, never by assuming which series was used.
notes.vintage_timing: INE published the revised population on 22 June 2026; the 2025 national accounts predate it and are expected to be rebenchmarked at a future benchmark revision.
notes.index_base_warning: The article's preliminary index is quoted on EU27_2025 = 100 (AMECO); Eurostat tec00114 is EU27_2020 = 100. Close, but not the same unit.
notes.world_bank_population: The World Bank population series tracks the national-accounts basis, not the revised demographic one. Kept for comparison, never used as 'the population'.
